# 🚀 GitHub API Client - Auto-Generated by UniStructGen

> **One OpenAPI spec → Full type-safe GitHub client in 5 minutes**

This example demonstrates the **revolutionary power** of UniStructGen: transforming a single OpenAPI specification into a production-ready, fully type-safe Rust API client with **automatic validation**.

---

## 🎯 What This Demonstrates

### ❌ **Traditional Approach** (Manual Hell)

```rust
// 1. Manually define types (200+ lines of boilerplate)
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct User {
    id: i64,
    login: String,
    // ... 15 more fields
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Repository {
    id: i64,
    name: String,
    // ... 30 more fields
}

// 2. Manual validation (another 100+ lines)
impl User {
    fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
        if self.login.len() < 1 || self.login.len() > 39 {
            return Err("Invalid login length");
        }

        let regex = Regex::new(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$")?;
        if !regex.is_match(&self.login) {
            return Err("Invalid login format");
        }

        // ... 20 more validation rules for each field
    }
}

// 3. Repeat for EVERY type (Issue, PullRequest, Repository, etc.)
// 4. Keep synchronized with GitHub API changes (manually!)
// 5. Write tests for validation logic
```

**Problems:**
- 😫 **500+ lines** of boilerplate for 10 types
- 🐛 Easy to miss validation rules
- 📝 Duplicate logic between code and docs
- 🔄 Manual sync when API changes
- ⏰ **4-6 hours** of tedious work

### ✅ **With UniStructGen** (Pure Magic)

```rust
// In github-api.yaml - Define types ONCE
User:
  type: object
  required: [id, login, type]
  properties:
    login:
      type: string
      minLength: 1
      maxLength: 39
      pattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$'

# ↓ UniStructGen automatically generates ↓

unistructgen_macro::openapi_to_rust! {
    file = "github-api.yaml"
}

// That's it! 🎉
// - All types generated ✅
// - All validation from OpenAPI ✅
// - Full type safety ✅
// - Zero boilerplate ✅
```

**Benefits:**
- ✨ **~450 lines** of code you DON'T write
- 🛡️ Type-safe at compile time
- 📖 OpenAPI spec = single source of truth
- 🚀 API always matches documentation
- ⚡ Changes in 1 file → updates everything

## 📦 What Gets Generated

From the `github-api.yaml` spec, UniStructGen automatically creates:

### 🎨 **10+ Fully Type-Safe Structs**

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, validator::Validate)]
pub struct User {
    pub id: i64,

    #[validate(length(min = 1, max = 39), regex = "^[a-zA-Z0-9]([a-zA-Z0-9-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$")]
    pub login: String,

    #[validate(length(max = 255))]
    pub name: Option<String>,

    #[validate(email)]
    pub email: Option<String>,

    #[validate(length(max = 160))]
    pub bio: Option<String>,

    pub r#type: UserType,  // Enum!

    #[validate(range(min = 0))]
    pub public_repos: Option<i32>,

    #[validate(range(min = 0))]
    pub followers: Option<i32>,

    pub created_at: Option<chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>>,

    #[validate(url)]
    pub html_url: Option<String>,

    // ... and more!
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum UserType {
    User,
    Organization,
    Bot,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, validator::Validate)]
pub struct Repository {
    pub id: i64,

    #[validate(length(min = 1, max = 100), regex = "^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$")]
    pub name: String,

    pub owner: User,  // Nested type!

    pub private: bool,

    #[validate(length(max = 350))]
    pub description: Option<String>,

    #[validate(range(min = 0))]
    pub stargazers_count: Option<i32>,

    #[validate(length(max = 20))]
    pub topics: Option<Vec<String>>,

    pub visibility: Option<RepositoryVisibility>,  // Enum!

    // ... 25+ more fields!
}

// Plus: Issue, PullRequest, Label, CreateIssueRequest,
//       CreateRepositoryRequest, and more!
```

### ✨ **Key Features (Auto-Generated)**

- ✅ **Validation Attributes** - All from OpenAPI constraints:
  - `minLength/maxLength` → `#[validate(length(...))]`
  - `pattern` → `#[validate(regex = "...")]`
  - `minimum/maximum` → `#[validate(range(...))]`
  - `format: email` → `#[validate(email)]`
  - `format: uri` → `#[validate(url)]`

- ✅ **Serde Derives** - Automatic serialization/deserialization
- ✅ **Enums** - Type-safe variants from OpenAPI enums
- ✅ **Nested Types** - Complex object hierarchies
- ✅ **Optional Fields** - Proper `Option<T>` handling
- ✅ **Date/Time** - `chrono::DateTime` support
- ✅ **Documentation** - Preserved from OpenAPI descriptions

## 🔍 Code Comparison

### Creating a Repository

#### ❌ Manual Approach

```rust
// Manual type definition
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct CreateRepoRequest {
    name: String,
    description: Option<String>,
    private: bool,
}

// Manual validation
impl CreateRepoRequest {
    fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
        // Validate name length
        if self.name.is_empty() || self.name.len() > 100 {
            return Err("Name must be 1-100 characters");
        }

        // Validate name pattern
        let regex = Regex::new(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$").unwrap();
        if !regex.is_match(&self.name) {
            return Err("Name contains invalid characters");
        }

        // Validate description length
        if let Some(desc) = &self.description {
            if desc.len() > 350 {
                return Err("Description too long");
            }
        }

        Ok(())
    }
}

// Manual request
let request = CreateRepoRequest {
    name: "my-project".to_string(),
    description: Some("My awesome project".to_string()),
    private: false,
};

// Manual validation call
request.validate()?;

// Finally make the API call
let repo = client.post("/user/repos")
    .json(&request)
    .send()?
    .json::<Repository>()?;

// Manual validation of response
repo.validate()?;
```

**Lines of code:** ~40+ lines (just for this one operation!)

#### ✅ With UniStructGen

```rust
// Types are already generated from OpenAPI spec! 🎉

use validator::Validate;

// Create request - types are auto-generated with validation!
let request = CreateRepositoryRequest {
    name: "my-project".to_string(),
    description: Some("My awesome project".to_string()),
    private: Some(false),
    has_issues: Some(true),
    auto_init: Some(true),
    ..Default::default()
};

// Validation happens automatically!
let repo = client.create_repo(request)?;

// That's it! Repository is validated and type-safe! ✅
```

**Lines of code:** 8 lines (and 300+ lines were auto-generated!)

**Difference:** **80% less code** + **100% type-safe** + **automatic validation**

## 🎨 The Magic Behind the Scenes

### Input: `github-api.yaml`

```yaml
CreateRepositoryRequest:
  type: object
  required: [name]
  properties:
    name:
      type: string
      minLength: 1
      maxLength: 100
      pattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$'
    description:
      type: string
      maxLength: 350
    private:
      type: boolean
      default: false
```

### Output: Auto-Generated Rust

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, validator::Validate)]
pub struct CreateRepositoryRequest {
    #[validate(length(min = 1, max = 100), regex = "^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$")]
    pub name: String,

    #[validate(length(max = 350))]
    pub description: Option<String>,

    pub private: Option<bool>,

    pub has_issues: Option<bool>,
    pub has_projects: Option<bool>,
    pub has_wiki: Option<bool>,
    pub auto_init: Option<bool>,
}
```

**You wrote:** 0 lines of this code
**UniStructGen generated:** All of it
**Result:** Compile-time type safety + runtime validation 🎯

## 📊 Complexity Handled

This example handles real-world complexity:

- ✅ **Nested Objects** - `Repository` contains `User`, `User` contains more fields
- ✅ **Enums** - `UserType`, `RepositoryVisibility`, `IssueState`
- ✅ **Arrays** - `Vec<Issue>`, `Vec<Label>`, `Vec<String>`
- ✅ **Optional Fields** - Proper `Option<T>` for nullable fields
- ✅ **Date/Time** - `chrono::DateTime<Utc>` for timestamps
- ✅ **URLs** - Validated URI fields
- ✅ **Email** - Email format validation
- ✅ **Regex Patterns** - Custom pattern validation
- ✅ **Numeric Ranges** - Min/max constraints
- ✅ **Array Length** - Max items validation

**All of this complexity is handled automatically!**
